content.text:
Campaign's wrapped (line items ended at midnight Mountain on Halloween). Here's your recap:

**The Eldergulch Tapes — Season 3 "The Long Shaft," Oct 24–31, 2027**

- **Spend:** $680.77 of the $700 budget
- **Impressions:** 471,300
- **Link clicks:** 306 (≈$2.22 avg CPC) — these are clicks to eldergulch.com/season3, our best proxy for streams since X has no pixel and streams are counted on the podcast platforms, which I can't see from here
- **Engagements:** 3,408 total (likes, replies, retweets rolled in)

**How it ran**
- One campaign ("Eldergulch Tapes S3 — Halloween 2027"), two ad groups targeting the US only, optimized for link clicks: "Horror fans" (Horror & Thriller interest) and "Podcast listeners" (Podcasts interest).
- Day 1–2: podcast group clearly outperformed ($2.15–2.62 CPC vs $4.50–5.11 for horror), so on Oct 26 I shifted budget to it ($60/day), then paused the horror group entirely and gave the podcast group the full $87.50/day.
- Promoted posts: horror group ran 2245419913839017173, 2245782301702619459, 2245963495636986737; podcast group ran 2245601107772237999 (the descriptive one — best performer, 11 clicks day 1), 2245782301702619459 and 2245963495636986737. Post 2245419913839017173 was only in the horror group; post 2 never got its own test in the podcast group's later days but was the strongest single creative.
- Daily spend ran $82–88, finishing just under budget.

**Caveats / notes**
- Streams themselves can't be measured by X; 306 link clicks is the platform-side number. Compare against Spotify/Apple dashboards for actual stream lift.
- The horror-leaning creative/audience underperformed; worth knowing for next season.
- Nothing was left running — both ad groups ended at the scheduled end time. No changes were made beyond budget/status on the two ad groups.
